title: Telling what happened
job: A four-sentence account in the past
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: dhahabtu ilā + al- + N + wa + V-perfect

rules.text: A verb placed BEFORE its subject stays SINGULAR: dhahaba al-awlād ilā as-sūq, never dhahabū al-awlād. It agrees in gender only. L1 dodged this entirely by using pronoun subjects, where the question cannot arise.

The perfect is Arabic's narrative tense and its person-suffix is written in full — dhahabtu, dhahabta, dhahabti, dhahaba, dhahabat. That is the one place the course's no-case-endings rule makes an exception, because the suffix carries the person and not the case.
kāna plus an adjective gives the standing situation: kāna al-jaww bārid. It is the whole of this level's background apparatus, and L1-M5 already taught the verb.

The two lines part company again: نسيت, ذهبت and قلت are one spelling each for two or three persons. The romanization carries the person and the script does not, which M1 first noticed and M8 met again.
An account is joined with thumma for order, wa for addition and lākin for contrast — all three already the learner's from M10 of the level below.

sentences.display: dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. kāna al-jaww bārid. ishtaraytu al-khubz. thumma dhahabtu ilā al-bayt.
sentences.script: ذهبت إلى السوق. كان الجو باردا. اشتريت الخبز. ثم ذهبت إلى البيت.
sentences.cue: I went to the market. The weather was cold. I bought the bread. Then I went home.
sentences.literal: I-went to the-market. Was the-weather cold. I-bought the-bread. Then I-went to the-house.

words.note: The perfect of M8's ashtarī from the level below, with the -tu that says "I". The Arabic line writes اشتريت for I and for you alike.

sentences.trap: Four sentences and no pronoun in any of them. The suffixes carry the person, and putting anā in front of each would read as insistence.
sentences.sound: ish-ta-RAY-tu, with the ay as in English "eye" and the stress before the ending.

variations.display: dhahabtu ilā as-sūq wa ishtaraytu al-khubz
variations.cue: I went to the market and bought the bread
variations.changed: two steps joined into one sentence

variations.cue: The weather was cold yesterday
variations.changed: the background line alone, with a time

variations.cue: I bought the bread from the market
variations.changed: min doing its first job, after three modules of others

mistake.display: anā dhahabtu ilā as-sūq. anā ishtaraytu al-khubz.
mistake.script: أنا ذهبت إلى السوق. أنا اشتريت الخبز.
mistake.why: The -tu already says who. Repeating anā in every clause is the English shape and reads as insistence.

sentences.usage: The ordinary account of a small errand. Four short sentences and one speaker, named nowhere.
sentences.mnemonic: The suffix says who; nothing else needs to.

sentences.display: ittaṣala ṣadīqī. kuntu fī al-bayt. takallamnā kathīran. kāna laṭīf.
sentences.script: اتصل صديقي. كنت في البيت. تكلمنا كثيرا. كان لطيفا.
sentences.cue: My friend called. I was at home. We talked a lot. It was nice.
sentences.literal: Contacted friend-my. I-was in the-house. We-spoke much. Was nice.

words.note: The perfect of M7's attaṣil, and it comes BEFORE its subject here — which is the ordinary Arabic order and the module's rule 0.
The perfect of M10's atakallam from the level below, with -nā for "we". Every person of the perfect is a suffix, and this is the one for us.

sentences.trap: The verb stands in front of its subject and that is normal. English cannot do it at all, so a learner reading ittaṣala ṣadīqī will look for the subject in the wrong place.
sentences.sound: it-TA-ṣa-la, with the t doubled and the ṣ emphatic.

variations.cue: My mother called yesterday
variations.changed: a feminine subject, so the verb takes -at

variations.display: kuntu fī al-bayt wa ittaṣala ṣadīqī
variations.cue: I was at home and my friend called
variations.changed: the background and the event joined with wa

variations.cue: We talked a lot and it was nice
variations.changed: the last two joined with wa

mistake.why: That is grammatical and puts the weight on the friend rather than on the call. Verb first is the neutral order for telling what happened.

sentences.usage: A phone call recounted, and the background line is what makes it a story rather than a list.
sentences.mnemonic: The verb goes first and the subject follows it in.

sentences.display: dhahaba al-awlād ilā al-madrasa. kāna al-jaww jamīl. akalū fī al-maṭʿam. rajaʿū fī as-sāʿa ath-thāniya.
sentences.script: ذهب الأولاد إلى المدرسة. كان الجو جميلا. أكلوا في المطعم. رجعوا في الساعة الثانية.
sentences.cue: The children went to school. The weather was lovely. They ate at the restaurant. They came back at two o'clock.
sentences.literal: Went the-children to the-school. Was the-weather lovely. They-ate in the-restaurant. They-returned at the-hour the-second.

words.note: SINGULAR even though the children are plural, because the verb comes first. Once the subject has been named the later verbs go plural: akalū, rajaʿū. The row for dhahaba is L1-M5's.
The perfect with -ū for "they", on M5's verb from the level below. It follows its subject here, so it agrees in full.
The perfect with -ū for "they", used here because the subject has already been named and the verb now follows it.

sentences.trap: dhahaba is singular and akalū is plural, in the same account, about the same children. Position decides: a verb before its subject stays singular, and one after it agrees.
sentences.sound: DHA-ha-ba, and ra-ja-ʿŪ with the stress on the ending.

variations.cue: The children went to the market
variations.changed: the first line alone, with the singular verb

variations.cue: The children went to school
variations.changed: the subject first, so the verb goes plural

variations.cue: My mother came back at four o'clock
variations.changed: a feminine subject after the verb, so it takes -at

mistake.why: A verb before its subject stays singular: dhahaba al-awlād. The plural belongs after the subject, as the second variation shows.

sentences.usage: The sentence the whole module is built to teach. The two variations put the rule's two halves side by side.

sentences.display: nasītu al-miftāḥ. rajaʿtu ilā al-bayt. kāna fī as-sūq. thumma ittaṣaltu bi-ṣadīqī.
sentences.script: نسيت المفتاح. رجعت إلى البيت. كان في السوق. ثم اتصلت بصديقي.
sentences.cue: I forgot the key. I went back home. It was in the market. Then I called my friend.
sentences.literal: I-forgot the-key. I-returned to the-house. Was in the-market. Then I-contacted with-friend-my.

words.note: The I-form of S03's rajaʿū. The row is S03's, and this is the person-suffix a first-person account needs.
The I-form of S02's ittaṣala, still needing bi- to reach the person called. The row is S02's.

sentences.trap: Three verbs in four sentences, all first person, and the Arabic writes the first two identically to their you-forms. The romanized line is the only one that says who.
sentences.sound: ra-JAʿ-tu and it-ta-ṢAL-tu, both stressed just before the -tu.

variations.display: nasītu al-miftāḥ, thumma rajaʿtu ilā al-bayt
variations.script: نسيت المفتاح، ثم رجعت إلى البيت
variations.cue: I forgot the key, then I went back home
variations.changed: two steps in one sentence

variations.cue: I called my friend yesterday
variations.changed: one step, with a time

variations.display: rajaʿtu ilā al-bayt fī as-sāʿa al-khāmisa
variations.script: رجعت إلى البيت في الساعة الخامسة
variations.cue: I went back home at five o'clock
variations.changed: M6's clock inside an account

mistake.why: Dropping the -tu changes the person to he. The suffix is the only thing carrying it.

sentences.usage: A bad morning in four sentences. thumma is what makes it a sequence rather than a list.
sentences.mnemonic: Change the suffix and you have changed who it happened to.

sentences.display: kāna ʿindī ṣudāʿ ams. kuntu fī al-bayt. nimtu kathīran. al-yawm anā bi-khayr.
sentences.script: كان عندي صداع أمس. كنت في البيت. نمت كثيرا. اليوم أنا بخير.
sentences.cue: I had a headache yesterday. I was at home. I slept a lot. Today I'm fine.
sentences.literal: Was at-me headache yesterday. I-was in the-house. I-slept much. The-day I well.

words.note: The perfect of M9's anām from the level below, and the long ā of nāma shortens to i before the suffix — nimtu. A shape to learn rather than derive.

sentences.trap: kāna ʿindī is how ʿind- reaches the past, because it is a preposition and cannot conjugate. M8 said so; this is where it is used.
sentences.sound: NIM-tu, one short syllable and the ending.

variations.display: kāna ʿindī ṣudāʿ, kuntu fī al-bayt
variations.script: كان عندي صداع، كنت في البيت
variations.cue: I had a headache, I was at home
variations.changed: the reason and the consequence in one sentence

variations.cue: I slept a lot yesterday
variations.changed: one step, with a time

variations.cue: Today I'm fine, thank goodness
variations.changed: M5's phrase closing the account

mistake.why: kāna comes first: kāna ʿindī ṣudāʿ. The verb heads the sentence, as rule 0 says.

sentences.usage: An account that ends in the present, which is what a story about being ill usually does.
sentences.mnemonic: ʿind- cannot conjugate, so kāna does it for them both.

sentences.display: qāla ṣadīqī: al-maṭʿam mumtāz. dhahabnā hunāka ams. akalnā samak. kāna ladhīdh.
sentences.script: قال صديقي: المطعم ممتاز. ذهبنا هناك أمس. أكلنا سمكا. كان لذيذا.
sentences.cue: My friend said: the restaurant is excellent. We went there yesterday. We ate fish. It was delicious.
sentences.literal: Said friend-my: the-restaurant excellent. We-went there yesterday. We-ate fish. Was delicious.

words.note: The perfect of "say", and its I-form shortens the ā the way nimtu does: qultu. Reported speech proper is a later level; here the words are simply quoted.
A step above jayyid, and the ordinary word for praising anything. It agrees like any adjective.
Of food only, where mumtāz praises anything. Both dh sounds are the dh of "this".
The -nā of takallamnā, on L1-M5's verb. The row for dhahaba is S03's.

sentences.trap: qāla ṣadīqī puts the verb first again, and what follows the colon is quoted rather than reported — Arabic's reported speech is a later level and this module does not touch it.
sentences.sound: QĀ-la, with the q at the back of the throat. mum-TĀZ, stressed on the long ā.

variations.cue: My mother said: the restaurant is excellent
variations.changed: a feminine subject after the verb

variations.cue: I said: the restaurant is near
variations.changed: the I-form, with its shortened vowel

variations.cue: We went there and ate fish
variations.changed: the middle two joined with wa

mistake.why: Grammatical, and it shifts the weight onto the friend. Telling what happened puts the verb first.

sentences.usage: Passing on a recommendation. The colon does the work reported speech would do in a later level.
sentences.mnemonic: Quote the words and you need no reporting grammar.

sentences.display: waṣaltu ilā al-maḥaṭṭa. kāna al-qiṭār mutaʾakhkhir. intaẓartu kathīran. thumma waṣala.
sentences.script: وصلت إلى المحطة. كان القطار متأخرا. انتظرت كثيرا. ثم وصل.
sentences.cue: I arrived at the station. The train was late. I waited a long time. Then it arrived.
sentences.literal: I-arrived to the-station. Was the-train late. I-waited much. Then it-arrived.

words.note: Arriving takes ilā, like going. The last sentence uses the bare he-form, waṣala, because the train has already been named.
The ẓ is emphatic and dark, and the initial i- is the same unwritten hamza as in ishrab and idhhab.
Of a thing or a person that has been delayed. The medial hamza is written ʾ, as in masāʾ and qaraʾtu.

sentences.trap: waṣaltu and waṣala in the same account, and only the suffix separates them. The Arabic line writes وصلت for the first and وصل for the second, so here the script does help.
sentences.sound: wa-ṢAL-tu and in-ta-ẒAR-tu, both stressed just before the ending.

variations.display: waṣaltu ilā al-bayt fī as-sāʿa ath-thāniya
variations.script: وصلت إلى البيت في الساعة الثانية
variations.cue: I arrived home at two o'clock
variations.changed: M6's clock inside the account

variations.cue: The train was late yesterday
variations.changed: the background line alone

variations.cue: I waited a long time, then the train arrived
variations.changed: the subject named at the end, with the verb still in front of it

mistake.why: Arriving takes ilā, as going does: waṣaltu ilā al-maḥaṭṭa.

sentences.usage: A journey recounted. Every verb here is a step and the one kāna sentence is the situation they happen in.
sentences.mnemonic: Arrive TO a place, not at one.

sentences.display: ishtaraytu kitāb ams. kāna ghālī lākin mumtāz. qaraʾtu kathīran. al-yawm anā saʿīd.
sentences.script: اشتريت كتابا أمس. كان غاليا لكن ممتازا. قرأت كثيرا. اليوم أنا سعيد.
sentences.cue: I bought a book yesterday. It was expensive but excellent. I read a lot. Today I'm happy.
sentences.literal: I-bought book yesterday. Was expensive but excellent. I-read much. The-day I happy.

words.note: The medial hamza is written ʾ and never a plain apostrophe. The q is at the back of the throat and the hamza is a catch in it.

sentences.trap: lākin joins two things that pull against each other, and it is M10's row from the level below. Nothing else in the sentence is new.
sentences.sound: qa-RAʾ-tu, with a clean catch of the throat before the ending.

variations.cue: I read the book yesterday
variations.changed: with the article, so it is a book already mentioned

variations.cue: It was expensive but excellent
variations.changed: the contrast alone

variations.cue: I bought a cheaper book
variations.changed: M9's comparative, inside an account

mistake.why: The medial hamza is written ʾ in this course, never a plain apostrophe: qaraʾtu. The two fold to the same key, and the display must carry one spelling.

sentences.usage: A small purchase recounted with a verdict on it, which is most of what people tell each other about.
sentences.mnemonic: Expensive but excellent — one lākin holds both.

sentences.display: dhahabat ummī ilā as-sūq. ishtarat al-fākiha. rajaʿat fī as-sāʿa ar-rābiʿa. kānat mutaʿaba.
sentences.script: ذهبت أمي إلى السوق. اشترت الفاكهة. رجعت في الساعة الرابعة. كانت متعبة.
sentences.cue: My mother went to the market. She bought the fruit. She came back at four o'clock. She was tired.
sentences.literal: Went mother-my to the-market. She-bought the-fruit. She-returned at the-hour the-fourth. She-was tired.

words.note: The feminine of dhahaba, and it comes before its subject — so it agrees in gender and stays singular. The row for dhahaba is L1-M5's.
The feminine of kāna, doing the same background job. The row for kāna is L1-M5's.
The feminine of ishtaraytu's verb, following its subject. The row for ishtaraytu is S01's.
A step beyond M5's taʿbān from the level below, and it agrees with whoever is tired.

sentences.trap: dhahabat before the subject, and every verb after it also feminine. Gender agreement survives the position rule; only NUMBER is suspended by it.
sentences.sound: dha-HA-bat and KĀ-nat, both ending in a fully released t.

variations.cue: My mother went to the school
variations.changed: a different destination

variations.cue: She was very tired
variations.changed: the last line alone, with jiddan

variations.cue: She bought the bread and came back
variations.changed: two steps joined with wa

mistake.why: Gender still agrees even when number does not: dhahabat ummī. The position rule suspends only the plural.

sentences.usage: An account about someone else. Notice that not one sentence after the first names her.
sentences.mnemonic: Position kills the plural, not the gender.

sentences.display: dhahabtu ilā al-maṭʿam maʿa ṣadīqī. akalnā kathīran. kāna al-ḥisāb ghālī. lākin kāna yawm jamīl.
sentences.script: ذهبت إلى المطعم مع صديقي. أكلنا كثيرا. كان الحساب غاليا. لكن كان يوما جميلا.
sentences.cue: I went to the restaurant with my friend. We ate a lot. The bill was expensive. But it was a lovely day.
sentences.literal: I-went to the-restaurant with friend-my. We-ate much. Was the-bill expensive. But was day lovely.

words.note: The -nā of takallamnā, on M5's verb from the level below. The row for akala is L1-M5's, and this is a cell of it.

sentences.trap: Nothing new is opened. Four sentences, three tenses' worth of work, and one new person-suffix on a verb the learner has had since L1-M5 — which is what a module's last item should look like.
sentences.sound: a-kal-NĀ, stressed on the long ending.

variations.cue: I went to the restaurant with my mother
variations.changed: a different companion

variations.display: kāna al-ḥisāb ghālī lākin kāna ladhīdh
variations.script: كان الحساب غاليا لكن كان لذيذا
variations.cue: The bill was expensive but it was delicious
variations.changed: the contrast made explicit on both sides

variations.cue: We ate a lot and came back
variations.changed: two we-forms in one sentence

mistake.display: anā dhahabtu, naḥnu akalnā, huwa kāna ghālī
mistake.script: أنا ذهبت، نحن أكلنا، هو كان غاليا
mistake.why: Every suffix already says who. Three pronouns in three clauses is the English shape and Arabic does not need one of them.

sentences.usage: The whole module in one item: an evening, four sentences, and a verdict at the end.
sentences.mnemonic: The endings carry the people; the account carries itself.
